notes: rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto sha3 (SHA3-224..512) and cshake (SHAKE and cSHAKE; empty name and customization give SHAKE, as in Go). Sha3 marshals Go's sha\x08 format by translating the sha3 crate's public SerializableState bytes; only the absorbing direction exists for it, so Go states whose direction byte is 1 (not producible from Go's public SHA3 API) are rejected. Shake.write fails with an io::Error where Go panics 'Write after Read'. Shake additionally implements std::io::Read and Clone.

SHAKE.AppendBinary.note: RustCrypto's cshake crate (0.2.1) keeps its sponge state private and implements neither SerializableState nor any accessor, so Go's sha\x09/sha\x0a state format cannot be produced without reimplementing the primitive, which ADR 0003 forbids

SHAKE.MarshalBinary.note: RustCrypto's cshake crate (0.2.1) keeps its sponge state private and implements neither SerializableState nor any accessor, so Go's sha\x09/sha\x0a state format cannot be produced without reimplementing the primitive, which ADR 0003 forbids

SHAKE.UnmarshalBinary.note: RustCrypto's cshake crate (0.2.1) keeps its sponge state private and implements neither SerializableState nor any accessor, so Go's sha\x09/sha\x0a state format cannot be produced without reimplementing the primitive, which ADR 0003 forbids
